headline: Integrated modeling resolves RNA folding and protein-driven DNA mechanics
label: Nucleic Acid Conformational Dynamics
summary: Recent preprints and papers pair force, single-molecule, and simulation data with structural models of RNA, DNA, and Cas9 conformational states.
synthesis: The common thread is conformational heterogeneity in nucleic acids and nucleic acid-protein complexes, probed by coupling experimental observables with computational models. In the RNA items, smFRET data guide integrative MD of a GNRA tetraloop-kissing contact, revealing bound and unbound coexistence at 10 mM Mg2+, while a multiscale framework combining adaptive MD and Markov state modeling maps RNA hairpin folding landscapes. MERGE-RNA fits secondary structure ensembles to DMS probing data using a physics-based maximum-entropy approach. For protein-nucleic acid systems, MD across seven Cas9 heteroduplex states defines a three-stage HNH activation pathway with a dynamically frustrated 18-nt checkpoint, and high-throughput magnetic tweezers resolve the MTERF1 polar roadblock through directional DNA unwinding. LOOP-TAG extends this to a massively parallel readout of length-dependent, protein-mediated DNA looping probabilities. The newer element is the combination of single-molecule or ensemble measurement with explicit kinetic and population-level modeling.
